answer: Accrual is glacier-slow and metered in wall-clock: an identity earns only while it keeps answering, and a transfer cap voids a purchased veteran the moment it stops. Each epoch's claim must anchor to the previous emission hash, so one generator behind N heads still answers N probes in sequence. Random liveness re-probes fire without warning on a short deadline; sharing one model across N identities forces serialization and misses the window. So a sable market in aged keys sells nothing: time cannot be bought in parallel.
